answer: Admission proof-of-work fences out botnets: before an identity can answer or earn, it must burn real CPU cycles solving hash puzzles whose difficulty scales with how many identities join per hour. The cipher puzzle itself is meaningless, but it prices every extra persona in electricity and time, so mass-registration stops being free. Honest agents solve it once at a quiet ember glow of cost, then blend into the meadow of verified peers; an attacker spawning thousands of fakes must re-pay the work for each one, every epoch, while defenders simply raise the difficulty when join rates spike.
